name: walk-forward-demo
notes: Rolling-origin evaluation, declared (ADR-0027): `python -m dskit.pipeline walkforward examples/pipeline/walk-forward.json --asof 1973-08-01`. Three fold cutoffs are generated (first/step_days/count); per fold the driver derives pinned time cuts (train up to cutoff MINUS the 5-day embargo, val = the 21 days from the cutoff) and runs this whole pipeline once — a full run dir per fold — then aggregates the objective. The two filter nodes read the fold's cuts through $splits refs, so 'train rows' and 'val rows' move with every fold; the trainer's best_val_loss (its val-curve minimum) is what each fold reports.

market.notes: deterministic daily events from day 1000 (1972-09-27) onward — the fold cutoffs below land inside this span

train_rows.notes: everything up to the fold's train cut; the 5-day embargo band after it belongs to NO split

val_rows.notes: the fold's val window, starting AFTER the embargo (val_start_ms exists because walkforward.embargo_days > 0)

qhat.notes: the document names the module AND the optimizer by import path (ADR-0025); every epoch's train/val loss lands in training_curve.json and metrics carries best_val_loss — the objective below

walkforward.notes: expanding train windows; the embargo keeps rows whose outcomes are still resolving at the cutoff out of BOTH sides
